claims.text:
30. temporal-split

Target / packet: ai-temporal-split · F2. Prerequisites: ai:data-leakage.

Nearest / distinct payoff: data-leakage → duplicates-in-the-test. Entity separation is held aside; this checks feature availability against prediction time, independently of whether a score happens to be high.

Finite primary model: At day t label is next day demand. Three prediction rows labels [0,1,0]. Declared leaky feature future label=[0,1,0] gives rule accuracy 3/3; available prior-day feature=[1,0,1] gives rule 0/3. Temporal admission allows only information timestamp<=prediction time.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: A legitimate past feature=[0,1,0] can also score 3/3: high score alone is not leakage evidence. Shuffling cannot make future facts available at the past prediction time.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict which feature admission rule excludes future label; recall timestamp before prediction permits accurate past signal.

Required observable evidence: Show prediction timestamp and each feature availability timestamp before scores; no invented trained forecast benchmark.

Source obligation: Declared local finite model. Exact results require independent arithmetic reproduction; this construction supports no real-model performance or universal improvement claim. Method-source obligations remain as listed in the acquisition record below.
